==Problem==
Nicolas is planning to send a package to his friend Anton, who is a stamp collector. To pay for the postage, Nicolas would like to cover the package with a large number of stamps. Suppose he has a collection of <imath>5</imath>-cent, <imath>10</imath>-cent, and <imath>25</imath>-cent stamps, with exactly <imath>20</imath> of each type. What is the greatest number of stamps Nicolas can use to make exactly <imath>\$7.10</imath> in postage?
(Note: The amount <imath>\$7.10</imath> corresponds to <imath>7</imath> dollars and <imath>10</imath> cents. One dollar is worth <imath>100</imath> cents.)

<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ 45 \qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 46 \qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 51 \qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 54\qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 55</imath>

==Solution 1==

Let's use the most stamps to make <imath>7.10.</imath> We have <imath>20</imath> of each stamp, <imath>5</imath>-cent (nickels), <imath>10</imath>-cent (dimes), and <imath>25</imath>-cent (quarters).

If we want the highest number of stamps, we must have the highest number of the smaller value stamps (like the coins above). We can use <imath>20</imath> nickels and <imath>20</imath> dimes to bring our total cost to <imath>7.10 - 3.00 = 4.10</imath>. However, when we try to use quarters, the <imath>25</imath> cents don’t fit evenly, so we have to give back <imath>15</imath> cents to make the quarter amount <imath>4.25</imath>. The most efficient way to do this is to give back a  <imath>10</imath>-cent (dime) stamp and a <imath>5</imath>-cent (nickel) stamp to have <imath>38</imath> stamps used so far. Now, we just use <imath>\frac{425}{25} = 17</imath> quarters to get a grand total of <imath>38 + 17 = \boxed{\textbf{(E)}\ 55}</imath>.

~apex304, SohumUttamchandani, wuwang2002, TaeKim, Cxrupptedpat, InterstellerApex, mahika99, RyanZ4552

==Solution 2==
The value of his entire stamp collection is <imath>8</imath> dollars. To make <imath>\$7.10</imath> with stamps, he should remove <imath>90</imath> cents worth of stamps with as few stamps as possible. To do this, he should start by removing as many <imath>25</imath> cent stamps as possible as they have the greatest denomination. He can remove at most <imath>3</imath> of these stamps. He still has to remove <imath>90-25\cdot3=15</imath> cents worth of stamps. This can be done with one <imath>5</imath> and <imath>10</imath> cent stamp. In total, he has <imath>20\cdot3=60</imath> stamps in his entire collection. As a result, the maximum number of stamps he can use is <imath>20\cdot3-5=\boxed{\textbf{(E)}\ 55}</imath>.

~pianoboy
